narrative: OMX30 faces a mixed overnight backdrop: European bourses (+0.33% avg) outperformed a weaker US close (S&P -0.45%, Dow -1.21%), and while USD/SEK strength (+0.41%) benefits Volvo, Atlas Copco and Ericsson, the index sits at 92% of 52-week range with MACD crossing below signal—a warning flag. The +5.9% bull-market premium over 200-MA remains intact, but RSI 41.75 sits neutral-to-low and ADX 32.8 shows strong directional bias with bearish DI dominance, suggesting weakness momentum may be building. Oil's -5.96% crash is a double-edged sword: relief for consumer/industrial input costs but headwind for commodity narratives. US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET is the key catalyst; any surprise could rekindle Fed-policy discussion and rattle tech/DCF-sensitive stocks. Recommendation: cautious positioning, watch for MACD recovery or RSI dip below 40 before committing long.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens on a tentative footing after US equity selloff overnight, though DAX/CAC strength (+0.52%, +0.20%) cushions downside. Key technical red flag: MACD has crossed below signal line (hist=-5.650) whilst RSI 41.75 sits in the mid-range—momentum exhaustion pattern despite bull-market setup. Support at 3085 (lower Bollinger), resistance 3180 (50-MA). USD/SEK +0.41% is a tailwind for industrials (Volvo B, Atlas Copco, Sandvik) and telco exporters; but Brent oil -5.96% and EUR/SEK -0.08% create cross-currents—H&M faces sourcing-cost headwinds. Banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken) benefit modestly from US 10Y +20bp, widening NIM. Boliden watch: copper +2.36%, gold -0.89%—mixed commodity signal. US Jobless Claims (14:30 CET) is the macro event risk; any hawkish surprise could accelerate tech/DCF compression. Range trade 3110–3160 most likely; break below 3100 on weak close would confirm mean reversion.
